lines.en: Excuse me! **Which line goes to** the art museum?
lines.pt: Com licença! Qual linha vai para o museu de arte?

lines.en: Take the blue line. It’s the B train.
lines.pt: Pegue a linha azul. É o trem B.

lines.en: Thanks! Oh, here it comes. **Does this go to** the museum?
lines.pt: Obrigada! Ah, ele está chegando. Este vai para o museu?

lines.en: Yes, it does. **Get off at** Park Street.
lines.pt: Sim, vai. Desça em Park Street.
Quatro paradas. Cerca de dez minutos.

lines.en: No, go ahead. It gets busy at five.
lines.pt: Não, pode sentar. Fica cheio às cinco.

pages.title: Taking the bus or subway

unit.name: Getting around
map: Renting a bike or a car

situation.text: You are new in the city and standing on a subway platform. You need to find the right line, check the train and know where to get off.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can ask which line to take, check that a train goes to your place, ask how many stops it is and know where to get off.
canDo: Check: Does this train go to…?
Ask: How many stops is it?
success: I ask which line to take.
I find out how many stops.
pages.think: How do you usually find the right bus or subway in your city? Do you ask people or use an app?

teach.goal: Abrir a aula pela situação real, não pela regra.
solo: Leia o objetivo em voz alta e peça que o estudante diga com as próprias palavras o que vai fazer hoje.
Pergunte “Think about it” antes de mostrar qualquer expressão.
group: Cada estudante diz UMA palavra que associa à situação de hoje.
Mostre os 4 critérios de sucesso: é a missão final da aula.
extra: How do you get around your city?
What is hard about taking a bus in a new city?
support: Aceite respostas curtas ou em português na primeira rodada e reformule em inglês.

pages.title: Connection & warm-up

intro.solo: Start with real questions about the student’s life, not a grammar test.
intro.group: One question per student, then a question back to a classmate.

pages.recall: Quick recall from the unit start: “I usually…”. Ask: How do you usually get to class or work?

qs.q: How do you get to work or class?
qs.pt: Como você vai para o trabalho ou a aula?

qs.q: Have you ever been lost on a bus?
qs.pt: Você já se perdeu em um ônibus?

pages.tip: Use the answers to find gaps and to recycle earlier content. The goal is to enter English from the first minute.

teach.goal: Entrar no idioma no primeiro minuto, retomar a aula anterior e mapear lacunas.
extra: Have you ever taken a subway in another country?
What is rush hour like where you live?

errors.w: I go to work by foot.

support: Ofereça as respostas-modelo (chips) e peça apenas que escolham uma.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Life in the USA
pages.intro: In big American cities, millions of people ride buses and subways. Look at the cards and guess before you read.

cards.en: Fare card or tap to pay
cards.pt: Cartão de passagem ou pagamento por aproximação
cards.note: Many systems let you tap a card or phone at the gate.
Early morning and late afternoon: trains and buses are very full.
Signs ask you to give these seats to older people or people with a disability.

qs.q: How do people pay for the bus or subway?
qs.pt: Como as pessoas pagam o ônibus ou o metrô?

levels.A2: They tap a card or a phone.
levels.B1: Many cities use a rechargeable card or let you tap a phone or bank card.
levels.B2: Payment varies by city: some use rechargeable cards, others contactless payment or exact change on buses.

qs.pt: O que é horário de pico?

levels.A2: It is the busy time, when people go to or leave work.
levels.B1: It is the busy part of the day, usually morning and late afternoon, when trains are crowded.
levels.B2: Rush hour is when commuting peaks, so service is more frequent but also much more crowded.

levels.A2: Older people and people who need help.
levels.B1: These seats are for older people, pregnant women and people with a disability.
levels.B2: People are expected to offer these seats to anyone who needs them more, even if the sign is not there.

pages.compare: In Brazil many buses have a fare collector or a card reader at the turnstile. In US cities, how you pay changes from one city to another. What is the system where you live?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto cultural e as primeiras hipóteses.
solo: Mostre os 3 cartões e peça hipóteses antes de explicar.
Peça que o estudante compare com a sua própria experiência no Brasil.
group: Cada estudante escolhe um cartão e explica em uma frase.
Pergunte “Do you agree?” entre colegas.
answers: Q1: card, phone or sometimes exact change.
Q2: horário de pico, manhã cedo e fim de tarde.
Q3: idosos e pessoas com deficiência (e gestantes).
extra: Do you give your seat to others? When?
support: Use as respostas do nível A1 como andaime e peça que repitam.
stretch: B2: compare as convenções do Brasil e dos EUA nesta situação.

teach.goal: Compreender a situação antes de ver o texto: ideia principal e depois as informações-chave.
solo: Esconda o texto. 1ª escuta: só a ideia principal.
2ª escuta: as informações da tarefa 2.
Mostre o texto só depois da 2ª escuta.
group: Escuta coletiva; duplas anotam as respostas antes de revelar.
Compare as respostas entre as duplas e só então mostre o texto.
answers: Pass 1: to find the right train.
Pass 2: blue line · Park Street · four stops · ten minutes.
extra: Who is speaking? How do you know?
Which word did you catch first?
support: Pause depois de cada fala se necessário.

qs.q: Which line goes to the museum?
What does she ask before she sits?

retell.prompt: Retell the conversation in your own words, at your level.

teach.goal: Ler o diálogo, perceber os chunks e recontar.
solo: O estudante lê um papel e você lê o outro; depois trocam.
Peça que reconte a conversa no nível que conseguir.
group: Leitura em duplas e troca de papéis.
Reconto em cadeia: uma frase por estudante.
answers: Blue line (B train) · Park Street · four stops · ask before sitting
extra: What would YOU ask a stranger on the platform?

errors.w: Where is the train that goes the museum?
errors.r: Which train goes to the museum?
Does this go to the museum?

support: Mostre a tradução (botão PT) depois da 2ª leitura.

pages.title: Useful expressions

items.use: Find the right line for your destination.
Check that the bus or train is the right one.
Ask how far your stop is.
Someone tells you where to leave the train or bus.
Someone tells you which line or bus to use.
Ask politely before you sit next to someone.
Thank someone who gave you directions.

items.en: Which line goes to the airport?

pages.note: Instead of memorizing the whole list, choose 3–5 expressions (★) to use again and again. The others are for understanding and for stretching later.

teach.goal: Escolher 3–5 chunks para uso repetido e descobrir a função de cada um.
solo: Pergunte “When do you say it?” antes de dar o significado.
Peça um exemplo próprio para cada expressão ★.
group: Cada estudante escolhe a expressão que mais usaria e explica quando.
Compare equivalentes formais e informais em duplas.
answers: Prioritárias: Which line goes to…? · Does this go to…? · How many stops…? · Is this seat taken?
extra: Which of these would you say to a friend? To a stranger?
support: Trabalhe só as expressões ★ nesta aula.

patterns.name: Which + noun
ex: Which line goes to the airport?
Which bus goes to the stadium?

patterns.name: Checking with does
ex: Does this train go to the museum?
Does this go to Main Street?

patterns.name: Counting stops
patterns.formula: **How many stops** + is it / to + place?
ex: How many stops to the airport?

head: Spoken English
Written English
rows: Does this service travel to the city center?
How many stops are there from here?
Yes, please feel free to sit.
register.note: These are differences of context and register, not absolute rules: signs and announcements use the more formal forms.

teach.goal: Fixar os padrões principais; os outros são expansão. Usar a troca de palavras para variar a fala.
solo: Mostre o padrão DENTRO do diálogo (grife os chunks).
Use “Swap the words”: toque em cada peça e peça que o estudante diga a frase completa.
Compare spoken × written em 2 exemplos.
group: Troca em cadeia: cada estudante muda UMA peça e o próximo repete a frase.
Em pares: um escolhe as peças, o outro fala.
teach.answers: Os padrões principais (main) são o foco; os demais são expansão para quem avançar rápido.
extra: Change one word and say the new sentence.

errors.r: I get off at Park Street.

support: Fique só com o primeiro padrão na primeira rodada.
stretch: Combinar dois padrões na mesma fala.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.focus: Word stress: strong and weak syllables
pages.tip: English has a beat. Strong words get a longer, louder beat. Little words like “to” and “the” are short and weak.

items.say: Which line goes to the airport?
items.linked: WHICH LINE goes to the AIR·port?

own.prompt: Write your own question about a bus or train in your city. Mark the strong words.
own.criteria: Say it twice: did the strong words sound longer and the small words short?

teach.goal: UM só fenômeno: Word stress: strong and weak syllables.
solo: 3 passagens: escutar e identificar → reproduzir ritmo e entonação → usar em frase com conteúdo próprio.
Modele devagar e normal; peça que o estudante bata palmas na sílaba forte.
group: Coro, depois duplas; circule ouvindo.
Cada estudante cria uma frase própria.
answers: Identify 1: Four stops. · Identify 2: Take the blue line.

errors.w: Todas as sílabas com a mesma força (ritmo de português)
errors.r: Sílabas fortes mais longas: WHICH LINE goes to the AIRport

support: Reduza a velocidade e conte as batidas em voz alta.

levels.h: Controlled practice — choose the best answer

items.q: 1. You are on the platform. You need the line to the airport.
opts: Which line goes to the airport?
Where is the airport line you?
items.why: Which line goes to…? asks for the right line.

items.q: 2. A train arrives. You are not sure it is the right one.
items.why: Does this go to…? checks the vehicle.

items.q: 3. You want to know how far your stop is.
items.why: Stops can be counted: How many stops…?

items.q: 4. A seat is free next to a stranger.
items.why: Is this seat taken? is the polite way to ask.

levels.h: Guided practice — complete, substitute and transform

items.why: Get off = leave the bus or train.

items.instr: Make it a question about stops:
Ask if the train goes to the stadium:
ans: Does this go to the stadium?
Does this train go to the stadium?
Does this go to the stadium
items.model: Does this train go to the stadium?

items.why: Thank the person when they help you.

teach.goal: Do controlado ao guiado: completar, substituir e transformar antes da fala livre.
solo: Peça que o estudante justifique cada resposta.
Se acertar rápido, peça a versão mais informal ou mais educada.
group: Resolvam em duplas e comparem antes de revelar.
Equipes: ponto por resposta justificada.
answers: 1: Which line goes to the airport? · 2: Does this go to downtown? · 3: How many stops is it? · 4: Is this seat taken?
Gap: Does · off · How many stops is it? · Does this train go to the stadium? · Thanks, that helps.
extra: Say each correct answer aloud with the right stress.
support: Ofereça o banco de palavras (chips) nas lacunas.

pages.title: Personalized roleplay — find your way underground

brief.teacher: You are a local at the station (add a change: the line is closed!).
brief.student: You are a visitor: ask which line to take and check the train.

orders: Go to a friend’s house on Main Street
complications: The line is closed today: take a bus.
The train is going the wrong way.
You are not sure which stop is yours.
The train is very crowded: ask about a seat.
success: I ask which line to take.
I find out how many stops.

teach.goal: Simulação com complicação inesperada e três rodadas com menos apoio.
solo: Combine o cenário com a vida do estudante (um lugar que ele realmente frequenta).
Rodada 1: com chunks. Rodada 2: só palavras-chave. Rodada 3: sem roteiro.
Meta de fala: 60–70% do tempo para o estudante. Anote 2–3 correções para a devolutiva.
extra: What if your train is cancelled? What do you say?

errors.w: Where is the train that goes the museum?
errors.r: Which train goes to the museum?

support: Volte à rodada 1 se travar; peça que repita só a primeira frase.
stretch: Peça que o estudante ajude outro “turista” (você) com as mesmas instruções.

rounds.title: Find the line
rounds.task: Ask which line goes to your place. Your partner answers.

rounds.title: Check the train
rounds.task: Your partner is on the train. Check it goes to your stop.
rounds.hint: Does this go to…? / How many stops…?

rounds.title: Solve a problem
rounds.task: The line is closed or you are on the wrong train.
rounds.hint: Which line goes to…? / Get off at…

rounds.title: Share routes
rounds.task: Whole group: each pair shares the best route they found.
rounds.hint: Take the… and get off at…

infogap.title: City subway map
infogap.instr: Ask your partner and complete your card. Do not look at the other card!

a.title: Rider A asks
a.task: You know the airport and the museum. Ask about the rest.

b.title: Rider B asks
b.task: You know the stadium and the beach. Ask about the rest.

teach.goal: Fluência por repetição da função com informações novas a cada rodada.
group: Troque os pares a cada rodada (A+B / C+D → A+C / B+D → A+D / B+C → grupo todo). Com 6 estudantes, três duplas simultâneas.
Sem salas simultâneas: interações sequenciais enquanto uma dupla apresenta.
Responsabilidade individual: cada aluno faz ≥1 pergunta e ≥1 resposta.
answers: Info gap: A tem Airport (red, 6) e Museum (blue, 4); B tem Stadium (green, 3) e Beach (yellow, 9). Cada um completa perguntando: Which line goes to…? How many stops…?
extra: Which line goes to the beach?
How many stops to the stadium?

errors.w: Which line goes to the airport? (sem the)
errors.r: Which line goes to the airport?

support: Entregue frases-modelo no chat da turma.

pages.title: Group mission — lost on the subway
pages.goal: Each group must get across the city by subway in English: find the line, check the train and get off at the right stop.

missions.mission: You want to go to the stadium. Ask which line to take, then check the train.
missions.constraint: Use “Which line…?” and “Does this go to…?”

missions.mission: You are on the train. Ask how many stops to the museum and where to get off.
The train is full. Ask about a seat and thank the person who helps.
missions.constraint: Use “Is this seat taken?” and “Thanks, that helps.”

teach.goal: Realizar algo com o inglês: o objetivo é resolver, não só falar certo.
group: Cada grupo recebe papel, restrição e missão. Alterne os papéis.
Progressão: 1ª rodada com frases de apoio, 2ª só palavras-chave, 3ª sem roteiro.
Observe e anote 2–3 correções prioritárias; devolutiva no fim.
answers: Modelo: “Which line goes to the stadium?” → “Take the green line.” → “Does this go to the stadium?” → “Yes. Three stops.”
extra: What if the other person does not understand you?
support: Dê o início de frase (“Start with”) em cada cartão.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short text message to a friend: tell them how to get to your place by subway.
pages.model: Hi Sam! **Take the blue line** to Park Street. **Get off at** Park Street. It’s four stops from the museum. See you soon!
checklist: I said which line to take.
I said where to get off.
I closed in a friendly way.
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea instead of rewriting everything.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta ligada à situação comunicativa.
solo: Peça o texto; corrija 2–3 pontos prioritários e mostre uma forma mais natural.
group: Cada estudante escreve; depois troquem os textos entre colegas e corrijam em duplas.
extra: Add one more detail to your text.

errors.w: I take the subway to go in the museum.
errors.r: I take the subway to the museum.

support: Dê o modelo e peça só para trocar os dados.

criteria.name: Fluency
criteria.desc: Mantém a comunicação sem interrupções excessivas.

criteria.name: Language use
criteria.desc: Utiliza adequadamente padrões, vocabulário e expressões.

criteria.name: Pronunciation
criteria.desc: É compreensível e usa ritmo e entonação adequados.

criteria.name: Interaction
criteria.desc: Responde, pergunta, esclarece e desenvolve a conversa.

interpret.text: Needs more support. Revisit the main patterns with guided practice before the next lesson.
Functional performance. Work on the lowest criteria in the next lesson.
Good control. Raise complexity and speed; add follow-up questions.
Strong performance. Move to a more demanding situation.

prompts.well: Example: You asked which line to take and checked the train clearly.
prompts.improve: Example: Make the strong words longer: WHICH LINE goes to the AIRport.
prompts.next: Example: Plan a route with a change of line and explain it without notes.

teach.goal: Avaliar o que o aluno conseguiu comunicar, não só os erros gramaticais.
solo: O estudante se autoavalia primeiro; depois você.
Feche com os três blocos: What you did well · What to improve · Your next challenge.
group: Dê um comentário por critério a cada estudante.
Cada um escolhe o próprio próximo desafio.
teach.answers: A rubrica é uma ferramenta interna de acompanhamento, não uma certificação CEFR.

tasks.prompt: Without notes: ask which line goes to the museum.
tasks.model: Which line goes to the museum?

tasks.prompt: A train arrives. You are not sure about it. What do you ask?

items: Record a 45–60 second audio: ask for a route in a subway station.
Write a short message telling a friend how to get to your home by bus or subway.
Review three expressions from the class and create your own examples.
Listen to the dialogue again and mark the strong words.

unit: Travel · ask · check in · find your way

teach.goal: Toda aula termina com uma produção observável.
solo: Sem consultar as anotações: construir uma pergunta, responder a uma situação e usar uma expressão nova.
group: Exit challenge individual; compare com o colega e combine a tarefa de continuidade.
teach.answers: Which line goes to the museum? · Does this go to downtown? · How many stops is it?
extra: Revisão espaçada: retomar na próxima aula, depois de uma semana e na missão de encerramento da unidade.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.say: Which line goes to the museum?
ladder.goal: Ask for a line with short phrases, models and pictures.

ladder.say: Does this train go to the museum? How many stops is it?
ladder.goal: Check the vehicle and the distance.

ladder.say: I think I’m on the wrong train. Could you tell me how to get to the museum?
ladder.goal: Explain a problem and ask for a new route.

ladder.say: I got on the wrong line by mistake. Which station should I change at to get back on track?
ladder.goal: Handle a route problem with detail.

ladder.say: Rather than backtrack, would it be quicker to cut across on the bus and rejoin the line at the next hub?
Had I checked the map first, I’d have spared myself this detour, but it did let me see a part of the city I’d never have found otherwise.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
solo: Mostre onde o estudante está e a próxima etapa.
group: Cada um escolhe a frase do próprio nível e a do próximo.
